 Judgment

This appeal is preferred by the appellant challenging the conviction judgment and order of sentence passed Crl.Appeal No.2559/2019 by the learned I ACMM, Bengaluru in C.C.No.10832/2015,
dated:16.11.2019 and prays to set aside the impugned judgment and to acquit the accused.
2. The appellant herein was the accused No.1 and respondent was the State before the trial court.
For the sake of convenience, parties would be referred to by the ranks they were assigned before the trial court.

3. Brief facts of the case are as under:

sentences.text:
The accused has been charge sheeted for the offences punishable under Sections 419,
420, 465, 468 and 471 r/w. Section 34 of IPC and under Sections 66, 66(C) and 66(d)
of Information Technology Act in C.C.No.10832/2015 (Crime No.369/2014 of Tilak Nagar Police Station, Bengaluru)

After filing the charge sheet, the charge has been framed against the accused for the offences punishable under Sections 419, 420, 465,
468 and 471 r/w. Section 34 of IPC and under Sections 66, 66(C) and 66(D) of Information Technology Act.
The accused No.1 has pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried.
The case is posted for prosecution evidence.

After completion of the trial and on hearing the arguments, the learned Magistrate has hold guilty of Crl.Appeal No.2559/2019 the offences charged against the accused and was pleased to convict the accused for the offences punishable under Sections 419, 420, 465, 468 and 471 r/w. Section 34 of IPC and under Sections 66, 66(C) and 66(D) of Information Technology Act.
4.
The appellant/accused No.1 has preferred this appeal on the following grounds :

It is contended that the impugned judgment passed by the trial court is illegal,
perverse, arbitrary and without application of mind.
In the present case, C.Ws.1 to 6 have not been examined i.e., the complainant, C.Ws.2 and 3 who had paid the amount to the accused persons are not examined.
Hence there is no evidence regarding payment to the accused persons.
As such, the impugned judgment is illegal and shall be set aside.
Further the evidence of P.Ws.5 and 6 is not related to this case.

Their evidence in the present case are the copies of their evidence deposed in C.C.No.20412/2015 which is being challenged before the appellate court in Crl.
Appeal No.2536/2019 pending on the file of CCH No.61, Bengaluru.
Further P.Ws.7 to 9 are the witnesses related to C.C.No.21124/2015 and they have not deposed anything about this case.
But nothing is there in their evidence.
Hence the conviction passed against him without any evidence is unwarranted and illegal.
Crl.Appeal No.2559/2019 C.Ws.1 to 6 have not been examined in this case.
No recovery has been made from the possession of the appellant.

Even though the appellant has not been charged for the offences under Sections 465 and 468 of IPC,
the learned Magistrate has convicted the accused for the alleged offences, which is against law.
The learned Magistrate has completely erred by convicting the appellant even though there is no absolute proof of evidence against him.
The guilt of the appellant is not proved beyond reasonable doubt.
The learned Magistrate has convicted the appellant on the basis of assumptions, in fact there is no proof regarding the payment of alleged amount to the accused.
Hence the appellant cannot be held guilty of the offences charged against him.
No amount was seized from the accused.
Hence prayed to allow the appeal by setting aside the impugned judgment passed by the trial court.
5. On service of notice, the learned Public Prosecutor has appeared on behalf of the State.

7. Heard.
8.

The points raised for consideration are as under:
1.
Whether the appellant has made out sufficient grounds to interfere Crl.Appeal No.2559/2019 with the impugned judgment and order of sentence passed by the trial court ?
2. Whether the appellant/accused has made out a ground to set off for the imprisonment already undergone by him in judicial custody ?
3. What Order?

9. My findings to the above points are:
POINT No.1 : Negative, POINT No.2 : Affirmative, POINT No.3 : As per final order,
for the following:
REASONS 10. POINT Nos.1 & 2:- Since both these points are interconnected to each other, they have been taken up together for discussion in order to avoid the repetition of facts.
11.
I have considered the complaint averments, oral and documentary evidence placed before the trial court along with appeal averments placed before this court, the arguments addressed by both the sides.

12. It is the specific contention of the appellant that the appellant/accused has not been charged for the offences under Section 465 and 468 of IPC for which he Crl.Appeal No.2559/2019 has been convicted.

In this regard, it is necessary to refer to the charge framed by the trial court dated:21.08.2018 which is for the offences under Sections 419, 420, 465, 468, 471 r/w. Section 34 of IPC and Sections 66, 66(C) & 66(D) of Information Technology Act.

In the charge it has been specifically alleged that the accused had misrepresented himself as a Member of Rajiv Gandhi University Counseling and assured that he would get a MBBS seat and created forged documents and also created fake e-mails in the name of University and cheated C.Ws.1 to 3 and due to misrepresentation and fraud, wrongfully took Rs.30,00,000/- from them to provide them a medical seat.
The charge has been rightly framed.
The accused No.1 is convicted for the offences punishable under Sections 419, 420, 465, 468 and 471 r/w. Section 34 of IPC and under Sections 66, 66(C) and (D) of Information Technology Act.
There is no technical error committed by the learned Magistrate.
13. It is the further specific contention of the appellant that the evidence of P.Ws.5 and 6 is not related to this case.

They have given evidence in C.C.No.20412/2015 which has been challenged in Santhosh Rai Alais Santhosh Alais ... vs Tilaknagar P S on 5 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/29023226/

sentences.text: While P.Ws.7 to 9 are the witnesses related to C.C.No.21124/2015 and they have not deposed Crl.Appeal No.2559/2019 anything about this case.
Hence on the basis of their evidence, the accused has been wrongly convicted by the learned Magistrate.
14. In view of the aforesaid contention, it is pertinent to refer to the evidence recorded by the learned Magistrate in C.No.10832/2015.
It is noted that P.W.5 is one Balakrishna, P.W.6 is Dinesh Kumar, P.W.7 is Arun Mittal, P.W.8 is Somashekar and P.W.9-Dr.Neelesh Parikh.
The deposition is signed by the witnesses and the learned Magistrate.
On perusal of the deposition, there is nothing to establish that the evidence of the said witnesses are not pertaining to this case.

Even otherwise it is necessary to refer to the charge sheet wherein C.W.7 is Balakrishna who has been rightly examined as P.W.5, C.W.10-Dinesh, S/o.Prahlad Rai has been examined as P.W.6, C.W.13-Arun Mittal who has been examined as P.W.7, C.W.20-Somashekar who has been examined as P.W.8 and C.W.12-Dr.Neelesh Parikh has been examined as P.W.9.
15.
On considering the aforesaid evidence and the charge sheet, it can be safely said that the learned Magistrate has rightly examined the charge sheet witnesses.
There is nothing on record to prove that they are not the witnesses in this case.
Hence the contention taken by the appellant cannot be accepted.
Crl.Appeal No.2559/2019 16.

In the present case, the victims are P.Ws.5 and 6, are the son and father & both of them have deposed in their evidence that the accused assured them to get them admission to Belgaum Mecical College and he demanded Rs.38,00,000/- and accordingly they paid Rs.38,00,000/- to the accused in August 2014 and thereafter in December 2014 they came to know that the admission had not taken place, so they approached the police and filed the complaint.
The accused has not repaid them the money and has not given them the MBBS seat.
Also they have identified the accused before the court through VC.

The learned Magistrate has rightly appreciated the evidence of P.Ws.5 to 9 and as there is incriminating material against them and also the prosecution has also placed convincing materials before the court to prove the guilt of the accused beyond reasonable doubt and the accused has been rightly convicted.

17. It is also observed by the learned Magistrate that the accused No.1 is in judicial custody till date in some other case, which is pending before the learned XII ACMM, Hyderabad and also several cases are pending against the accused for the same offences in C.C.No.10832/2015,
C.C.No.30400/2015 and C.C.No.20412/2015 of Tilak Nagar Police Station.

The learned Magistrate has observed that on perusal of the Crl.Appeal No.2559/2019 order sheet, the accused had obtained statutory bail as per order of the court dated:9.03.2015 and he was produced under body warrant.
Further after the accused being convicted for the offence while hearing regarding the sentence, it was submitted by the advocate for accused that the accused is in judicial custody and sought to give set off for the period during which he is in judicial custody.

While passing the order for sentencing,
the learned Magistrate has observed in page No.37 of the judgment that the accused No.1 is in judicial custody in some other case and he is not entitled for set off out of sentence of imprisonment Santhosh Rai Alais Santhosh Alais ... vs Tilaknagar P S on 5 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/29023226/
4 imposed on him for the alleged offences.

sentences.text: 18. In this regard it is pertinent to note that during the pendency of the appeal, the counsel for the appellant filed memo stating that the appellant has undergone sentence imprisonment of 2 years 01 month 21 days.
Hence, submitted that the judgment of the trial court be confirmed and imprisonment already undergone by the appellant/accused be set off and appeal be disposed off accordingly.
Learned Public Prosecutor submitted that he has no objection and endorsed the same on the memo regarding the confirmation of the order passed by the trial court in C.C.No.10832/2015.
Crl.Appeal No.2559/2019 19.

In view of the observation made by the learned Magistrate in C.C.No.10832/2015 and the submission made by the learned advocate for accused in this case, it is necessary to refer to the order sheet in C.C.No.10832/2015 as to whether the accused was in judicial custody or not.

It appears that on 7.07.2018 the court was informed that the accused was in custody in some other case and UTP No.4954/2018 was furnished by the jurisdictional police and the learned Magistrate has issued body warrant against him and on 13.07.2018 the accused was produced under body warrant.
Hence it can be safely said that the accused was not in judicial custody in this case.

20. Even otherwise on perusal of the order sheet in Crime No.369/2014 pertaining to C.C.No.10832/2015 it is observed that on 9.01.2015 the Investigating Officer had filed a requisition stating that the accused Santhosh Rai @ Raghav Mishra is in judicial custody in Crime No.294/2015 and his UTP No.13312/2014 and accordingly body warrant was issued against him.

On 14.01.2015 the accused was produced before the learned Magistrate and the jurisdictional police have taken him to the police custody from 14.01.2015 to 23.01.2015.
21.
On 23.01.2015 the accused was produced before Crl.Appeal No.2559/2019 the court and was taken to the judicial custody.

Hence it can be safely said that the accused was in judicial custody from 23.01.2015 and it is not clear as to how the accused was again shown to have been produced under "body warrant" in C.C.No.10832/2015.
22.
On 13.10.2015 it is noted in the order sheet that the accused is not produced under body warrant and is reported to have escaped from custody, hence N.B.W., was issued against him.
Also NBW and proclamation was issued against the accused.
Thereafter as discussed supra, the accused was produced under "body warrant" on 13.07.2018.
On 26.07.2018 it appears that the accused was produced under custody, on 8.08.2018 his bail application was rejected.

But in the order sheet entries dated:21.08.2018, 3.09.2018, 17.09.2018, 29.09.2018, 2.11.2018, 15.11.2018, 28.11.2018,
10.12.2018, it appears that the accused was in judicial custody.

Hence it appears that again in the year 2019 the accused was produced from judicial custody through VC.
23.

Here itself, it is necessary to note that the judicial custody means a person being kept in prison on the orders of the Magistrate before whom the criminal case against him is pending and in judicial Santhosh Rai Alais Santhosh Alais ... vs Tilaknagar P S on 5 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/29023226/
5 custody the accused becomes the responsibility of the court.

sentences.text: While Crl.Appeal No.2559/2019 body warrant i.e., production warrant is a court order to bring an accused already in custody in another case to another court for production.
The Magistrate in front of whom he is produced under body warrant has no direct custody of the accused.
Hence judicial custody and producing under body warrant are two distinct proceedings and same cannot be overlapped.

In this case from the entries in the order sheet, it appears that the learned Magistrate has taken the judicial custody when he was produced before him whether it is in compliance of procedural of law or not cannot be looked into by this court at this stage, but taking note that the accused was in judicial custody as stated by the learned advocate for the accused for which the learned Public Prosecutor has submitted no objection.
24.
In view of the discussion mad supra, it is held that the accused has not made out a ground to set aside the conviction judgment passed by the learned Magistrate.
Further appellant/accused has made out a ground to set off for the imprisonment already undergone by him in judicial custody.
Accordingly, the Point No.1 in the Negative and Point No.2 in the Affirmative.

25. POINT No.3 : In view of my findings on Point Nos.1 and 2 as above, I proceed to pass the following :
Crl.Appeal No.2559/2019 ORDER The Crl. Appeal filed by the appellant is hereby dismissed.
Consequently, the impugned judgment passed by the learned I ACMM, Bengaluru in C.C.No.10832/2015, dated:16.11.2019 stands confirmed.
Further the imprisonment undergone by the accused is given set off.
Send back the records to the trial  court along with the copy of this  judgment.
